item.title: Rachel DeMita names one ‘diabolical’ decision by WNBA involving the Atlanta Dream
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/TGL/TGL via Getty Images Rachel DeMita has criticised the decision to have Atlanta Dream co-owner Renee Montgomery involved in USA Network’s post-game coverage during the 2026 WNBA Finals, questioning the optics of the arrangement. Montgomery served as a studio analyst while her own franchise competed against the Golden State Valkyries for the championship, raising questions among fans about potential bias. The series ended with Golden State claiming its first WNBA title after beating Atlanta 68-63 in Game 7, completing an impressive championship run in just the franchise’s second season. Rachel DeMita questions Renee Montgomery’s dual role during WNBA Finals Reacting to Montgomery’s involvement in the coverage, DeMita wrote on social media: “having one of the Dream’s owners host the post game show is actually diabolical 😰” The comment reflects concerns over the decision to place someone with a direct stake in one of the competing teams in a prominent broadcasting role during the Finals. Montgomery, a former WNBA player who spent 11 years in the league, has defended her ability to separate her ownership responsibilities from her work as an analyst. Speaking to Front Office Sports , she explained that her experience as a player helped her assess performances fairly, regardless of which team was involved. “I love the sport so much that you have to cover it a certain way,” Montgomery said. “Like I understand the effort, I understand the grind, I understand all the sacrifice that went into a player having a good game. So whether or not that player is playing for the Atlanta Dream doesn’t matter. I have to analyze the game for what I see.” She also said she had not been given specific restrictions by USA Network or her other employers. The debate comes as the WNBA continues to attract attention around its broadcasting and growing audience. Montgomery’s situation has also drawn comparisons with other high-profile cases involving sports analysts who hold ownership stakes in teams. However, the Finals ultimately belonged to Golden State. Gabby Williams scored 30 points in the decisive game, including a dominant second-half performance, as the Valkyries secured a 68-63 victory. Atlanta had another chance to claim a championship but fell short in a tense finish. The Valkyries, meanwhile, became champions in only their second season, giving their supporters a historic result to celebrate. item.title: Hansi Flick talks substituting Lamine Yamal and Frenkie de Jong the center-back after Barcelona beat Alaves
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 31: Hansi Flick, head coach of FC Barcelona, looks on during the Spanish league, LaLiga EA Sports, football match played between FC Barcelona and Deportivo Alaves at Spotify Camp Nou stadium on October 31, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Hansi Flick spoke about substituting Lamine Yamal after Barcelona’s 6-1 thrashing of Alaves on Saturday night at Camp Nou. Yamal scored twice in the game but was replaced after 74 minutes as Flick looked ahead to games against Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid. Flick is often reluctant to substitute Yamal but said it’s a lot easier after he’s scored two goals in a match. “When you score two goals, it’s easier to go out,” he told reporters. “I spoke with him at half time [about managing his minutes]. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half [is good], but it also important he has less minutes. “For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermín, Rapha. This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way.” Flick also spoke about playing Frenkie de Jong and Brian Farinas in defence due to the current injury problems he has regarding his backline. “At the moment we have to think different,” he added. “Four defenders are out in Xavi Espart, Andreas [Christensen], Jules [Koundé] and Eric Garcìa. Hopefully some will come back, but we don’t know when yet. So I asked Frenkie if he’s able to play there; he said ‘Yes, when I can help the team I will do it.’ “The same with Brian. I don’t know if he ever played [at right-back], maybe in La Masia, but he also played a good level. I am happy for him. He deserved these minutes, this game. He is focused, top in training, very professional. This is what we want from him and the players.”

item.title: Super Sakala, King of Sudair Derby as Al Fayha win in style
item.description: Super Sakala, King of Sudair Derby as Al Fayha win in style news Hosts take local bragging rights thanks to emphatic 4-1 victory against Al Faisaly, with Zambian forward getting goal and two assists You could see how much it meant to Fashion Sakala. To everyone at Al Fayha and the club’s supporters, too. The hosts in Al Majma’ah triumphed in the Roshn Saudi League’s first Sudair Derby in almost five years. Not only that, but they swept aside Al Faisaly, defeating their local rivals 4-1 at Al Majma’ah Sports City Stadium on Saturday night. They’d even trailed 1-0, Abdulrahman Al Safari putting the visitors in front right on the half hour. But then Al Fayha took over. Fashion Sakala equalises for Al Fayha in Sudair Derby against Al Faisaly They were led, as is so often the case , by super Sakala. The hugely popular Zambian equalised just before half time, then assisted Jason for Al Fayha's third not long after Ziyad Al Shafai had put Fabio Carille's men ahead. In injury-time, Sakala set up his side’s fourth, creating one for Hugo Moura to round off the night. To wrap a decisive derby display. At the final whistle, Sakala celebrated loudly in front of the Al Fayha fans. He embraced each and every one of his teammates. He joked with the coaching staff, even danced a little jig with one. He, of course, flashed that trademark wide smile . Soon collecting the Man of the Match award, a fourth of the 2026-27 RSL already, Sakala spelled out just how important a win it was - Al Fayha’s first in eight league matches and only their second in nine against Al Faisaly. Al Fayha star Fashion Sakala picks up Man of Match award for lead role in Sudair Derby win against Al Faisaly "We played very well," Sakala said. "The team did so much. We deserved to win this game - I'm very proud for the three points. This was the topic the whole week." Regarding his equaliser, a left-footed rocket from the angle, Sakala said: "I’ve scored some great goals with my left foot; in fact, I think I’ve scored more with my left than with my right. "I played more as an out-and-out striker in the second half. In the first half, I was playing on the wing. About 30 minutes in, the coach changed my role, moving me to the center-forward position. "We exploited that well, By staying up front, I knew I’d only be marked by one defender - and I knew that would cause him a lot of trouble." It did indeed. Al Fayha's star man had shone once more. item.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to extend MotoGP lead
item.description: Marc Marquez won the first of his seven MotoGP titles in 2013 [Getty Images] Reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix to take a 44-point lead over title rival Jorge Martin, who missed the race with injury. It was Marquez's first win in Malaysia since 2018, while his brother Alex finished third behind Pedro Acosta. Marquez, who has won the MotoGP championship seven times, moved up to 399 points after winning by over four seconds. The Spaniard will seal the title with two rounds remaining if he is able to extend his lead to 74 points at the Qatar Grand Prix next week. "We did a perfect race, so I'm super, super happy," said Marquez. "But my mentality still cannot change. I have to keep focus, keep pushing. There are not many races to go, but there are many moments left. So, we must be super confident." The Marquez brothers scrapped for the lead early in the race before the eventual winner pulled ahead, leaving Alex to tussle for the remaining podium places with Acosta. Marquez's compatriot Martin, who won the championship in 2024, tried to ride in the morning practice session but had to withdraw as he struggled with the fractured wrist suffered during a crash at last week's Australian Grand Prix.

item.title: Man United weigh up Ivan Toney move to ease striker issues
item.description: Man United weigh up Ivan Toney move to ease striker issues Manchester United are considering a move to sign Ivan Toney from Al-Ahli to ease the club’s centre-forward issues. Benjamin Sesko has been ruled out until January with an ongoing shin issue, with the Slovenian striker yet to start a Premier League game this season. Bryan Mbeumo has featured through the middle as an alternative, with United lacking recognised options. As a result, United are assessing options for January. CaughtOffside claim Toney is on the club’s radar, after a move for Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was deemed unrealistic. The former Brentford forward has scored 83 goals in 105 games since a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia in 2024, and has twice won the AFC Champions League with Al-Ahli. He’s understood to be happy in the Saudi Pro League, but would consider a Premier League return for the right offer. The 30-year-old has previously attracted interest from Tottenham Hotspur and Everton, though a massive contract in Saudi Arabia complicates a return to England. Toney reportedly earns a tax-free base salary of around £400,000 at Al-Ahli. But you could just tell pretty early on it wasn’t going to happen, and then he got it rolled on a couple times. Got to get him better, got to get him healthy. It’s unfortunate because he was having a tremendous year.” Right now, it’s unclear whether Rutgers will have Lonergan or Duff back healthy at any point in the final four games, starting with its Nov. 7 road contest at Wisconsin. The Scarlet Knights saw what it was like not having them healthy against Michigan. It wasn’t easy. “You’re talking about playing that game without your starting quarterback and without your best player,” Schiano said. “I thought our guys battled their guts out.” This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: Here's the status of Rutgers football QB Dylan Lonergan, star WR KJ Duff

item.title: Arteta says midfielder’s new contract is only a “matter of time”
item.description: Arteta says midfielder’s new contract is only a “matter of time” Mikel Arteta has given a positive update on Declan Rice’s Arsenal future, while stopping short of saying a new contract has already been agreed. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Mikel Arteta believes Declan Rice wants to stay at Arsenal for the long term and says it is only “a matter of time” before his future is sorted. Asked about the prospect of a new contract for his star midfielder whose deal expires in 2028 (although it comes with an option for an addition year), Arteta said : “My feeling is that he’s very happy here, in every conversation I have with him, and he wants to continue here for the long term. “It will be a matter of time before we sort that. He’s been very consistent again. “What we are demanding him to do every year is very difficult to maintain. He’s doing it, a big credit to him.” Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images For Premier League Rice joined from West Ham United in a club-record transfer in 2023 and has become an integral part of Arteta’s side. The 27-year-old missed Arsenal’s midweek shambles against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup with a small issue but is back in training ahead of Arsenal’s game against Liverpool on Sunday as they go in search of their first league win at Anfield in 14 years. Should he play, it would be his 171st appearance for Arsenal. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images

item.description: Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe 3rd T20I prediction, lineups and Sharjah pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sharjah’s roof took a pounding on Thursday night. Sikandar Raza cleared it with the last ball of Zimbabwe’s reply, his ninth six, and still finished 19 runs short. Afghanistan had been 38 for 5 when Azmatullah Omarzai and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai came together, and the pair added 142, the biggest stand for the sixth wicket or lower in T20Is. Omarzai went on to 116 off 50 balls with twelve sixes, before Rashid Khan hit three successive sixes in the final over to make it 221 for 7. They lost four wickets for fewer than 20 runs on Thursday and still won comfortably, which says plenty about the depth and nerve in their dressing room. Zimbabwe’s problem is structural. Evans and Matigimu took early wickets and then bled runs when it mattered, and a side with only one proven big hitter cannot keep up with side that has some serious batters. item.title: Jeff Ekhator hands Luciano Spalletti a huge fitness boost
item.description: Jeff Ekhator hands Luciano Spalletti a huge fitness boost Jeff Ekhator has returned to full training, providing Luciano Spalletti with a timely fitness boost as Juventus prepare for a crucial match against Napoli . The striker’s recovery comes at an important moment for the Bianconeri, who are struggling to secure victories. Juventus have entered a training retreat ahead of Napoli’s visit to Turin this weekend. The fixture is viewed as a must-win encounter, and the club need every available player to be at their best as they look to improve their recent results. Ekhator’s recovery Juventus signed Ekhator in the summer as one of the most promising teenagers in Europe. However, his first appearance for the club in pre-season, against Basel, ended in injury, and he has been working his way back to full fitness since then. The striker suffered a setback when he was close to returning at the end of August. As a result, Juventus decided not to rush his recovery, and they were prepared to allow him as much time as necessary, even if that meant waiting until next year. According to Tuttojuve , Ekhator has now recovered and is participating in full training. His return gives him an opportunity to be involved when Juventus face Napoli, although it remains to be seen whether he will be included in the matchday squad. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) A timely option The match against Napoli will be difficult, but Ekhator’s availability would give Spalletti another option from the bench. Juventus need players who can make an impact when required, and the striker’s return adds depth to the attacking options available to the coach. Ekhator’s recovery is also a positive sign for Juventus beyond this weekend. After months of rehabilitation and a setback that delayed his progress, the club can now consider integrating him back into the squad rather than continuing to wait for his return. Juventus will hope that Ekhator can contribute when called upon, even if he is not ready to start. His presence in full training is a welcome development for a team that needs results, and it gives Spalletti an additional player to consider as he prepares for a demanding fixture.

item.title: Just Arsenal, Ray Parlour and AI Glasses: Fun At The Oakley Meta Partnership Launch
item.description: Just Arsenal, Ray Parlour and AI Glasses: Fun At The Oakley Meta Partnership Launch Just Arsenal was invited to North London on Thursday for the launch of Arsenal’s new partnership with Oakley Meta, and it turned into a memorable morning of football, technology and conversation with Arsenal legend Ray Parlour. The event took place at The Gunners Pub, a familiar location for supporters, where the new Oakley Meta Vanguard glasses were part of a celebration of Arsenal’s connection with its fans. The launch centred on We Go Again , a new film featuring Declan Rice returning to the streets of North London along Arsenal’s title-winning parade route. Wearing the Oakley Meta glasses, Rice revisits the celebrations while looking ahead to the challenges still to come. The message is simple: enjoy success, but never stop striving for more. Trying the Oakley Meta glasses firsthand Having travelled into London to attend the event, I was particularly interested in experiencing the technology for myself. The glasses were set up through the Meta AI app on my phone, and I was able to try out the voice controls, take photographs and record video without needing to hold a camera. I have to say, I was impressed. The image quality was excellent, and being able to capture photographs and videos simply by speaking opens up some interesting possibilities, particularly for people creating content. There are additional features, including messaging and music integration, which I am still exploring, but my first experience was certainly positive. Arsenal ‘s new partnership with Oakley Meta is about more than the glasses themselves. The We Go Again campaign connects the technology with the club’s supporters, its North London roots and the determination to keep building on success. Ray Parlour shares his Arsenal memories and hopes for the future The appearance of Ray Parlour gave the event something particularly special for Arsenal fans. Ray was in excellent form, entertaining those attending with stories about his playing days, Arsène Wenger, the Invincibles and Arsenal’s famous 5-1 victory away to Inter Milan. There were plenty of laughs, particularly when he recalled captaining Arsenal for that remarkable victory and joking about why he wasn’t made permanent captain afterwards! But what stood out was how passionate he remains about Arsenal today. When asked about watching the current side as a supporter, Ray said: “I’m kicking every ball still. I’m in the stands, you know. item.title: Barcelona learn €70-80 million price tag for 27-year-old Tottenham star – report
item.description: Barcelona learn €70-80 million price tag for 27-year-old Tottenham star – report Barcelona have found themselves in a difficult situation in recent weeks, with the defence suffering a number of injuries. Hansi Flick is without Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart through injury. This has forced the German manager to get creative and start Frenkie de Jong at centre-back and Brian Farinas at right-back against Deportivo Alaves. However, this has also prompted the Catalan club to realise that their defensive depth is far from sufficient and that they may have to enter the transfer market. One player Barça have been linked with is Pedro Porro. Joan Laporta is said to be a huge fan of the Spanish right-back, although a January move is considered improbable. Tottenham’s asking price complicates Barcelona interest According to Diario SPORT , Tottenham would demand around €70-80 million to consider selling the 27-year-old defender. That valuation would prove to be a major obstacle for Barcelona. Spending that much money on a right-back might not be feasible given the club’s current financial situation. Tottenham are set to demand a huge fee for Pedro Porro. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Porro is one of Tottenham’s most important players. He recently signed a long-term contract with the London club until 2031. Spurs have full control over his contractual situation and can afford to call the shots in these negotiations. Both Barcelona and Real Madrid have been linked with the defender, and Porro has admitted that he would love to return to Spain at some point in his career. Is Porro worth such an investment for Barcelona? From a sporting perspective, Porro offers qualities that make him a tailor-made right-back for Hansi Flick’s team. His attacking instincts, energy and experience would make him an excellent option. His partnership with Lamine Yamal for the national team is another factor. Pedro Porro has an excellent relationship with Lamine Yamal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The duo combined very well during the World Cup and made the right flank their own for La Roja . However, spending up to €80 million on a right-back would be a significant decision. Barcelona’s priority has to be to sign an elite centre-back. Such a central defensive signing will not come cheap, and Barça need to pick and choose their battles in the transfer market. Even if the financial situation is not as precarious as it once was, the Catalan club cannot become reckless in the market. As ideal as Porro is, Barcelona should not consider a move for him unless Tottenham lower their demands.

item.title: Real Madrid learn how much they will have to pay to sign World Cup winner – report
item.description: Real Madrid learn how much they will have to pay to sign World Cup winner – report Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with many of their signings slowly starting to come good under Jose Mourinho. One position that has been problematic for the Portuguese manager in these early days is right-back. Both Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold have failed to make the position their own, and Mourinho has started using captain Fede Valverde at right-back for better balance. While the Uruguayan midfielder is doing a great job in his new role, Real Madrid may want to look for a long-term solution to free up their captain to play in midfield. One player Los Blancos have been linked with is Tottenham Hotspur star Pedro Porro. Tottenham determined to protect their prized defender Now, according to Diario SPORT , the north London club have placed a €70-80 million valuation on the 27-year-old defender. It is quite a steep figure for the Spanish World Cup winner and one that would make Real Madrid think twice. Pedro Porro has been linked with a future move to Real Madrid. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Porro’s contractual situation gives Spurs a lot of control. The Spaniard recently signed a deal with Tottenham until 2031. With no immediate pressure to sell, Tottenham can remain steadfast in their asking price and look to extract as much money as possible from a sale of Porro. The 27-year-old has already admitted that he would love to return to Spain at some point in the future, with both Barcelona and Real Madrid interested. Does Porro make sense for Real Madrid? Porro joined Spurs from Sporting CP a few seasons ago and quickly established himself as one of the best right-backs in the league. His attacking output, crossing and energy to race up and down the flank would make him an attractive proposition for any club. However, with Dumfries and Trent still in the squad, Los Blancos would struggle to justify such an expensive investment in another player. Trent Alexander-Arnold is having a difficult time at Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Real Madrid must first sort out their right-back situation and make a decision on the futures of the two stars before making a call on Porro. Dumfries only arrived from Inter Milan in the summer, and it would be too early to make a decision on him. Trent, on the other hand, has had a torrid 18 months in the Spanish capital and could push for an exit next summer. If the stars align and the opportunity presents itself, Los Blancos would have good reason to make a move for Porro. However, for now, the squad’s composition makes a potential move for the 27-year-old difficult, and it remains to be seen how this saga develops.

item.title: Sensational goal-scorer is coming to Liverpool's first-team, Andoni Iraola will love him
item.description: Sensational goal-scorer is coming to Liverpool's first-team, Andoni Iraola will love him Liverpool will be adding an exciting new attacker to their ranks very soon. Andoni Iraola's start to his career at Anfield has been very exciting so far. Liverpool are playing like the fans have wanted them to play for over a year. Iraola's football is quick, attacking and exciting to watch. More importantly, Iraola has had a knack for bringing the best out of the club's burgeoning young players. Lewis Koumas is playing out of his skin. Rio Ngumoha is finally ascending to the upper echelons of the footballing world, and Trey Nyoni has established himself as an absolute superstar in the middle of the park. The exciting part is that there are so many young players ready to break through, some are even more talented than those in the first-team right now. Liverpool's exciting attack It was so frustrating last season when Liverpool were filled to the brim with exciting attacking talent but Arne Slot could simply not get the best out of them. Under Iraola things are different. Alexander Isak is actually playing well and scoring goals. The wingers are all making important contributions. Aside from Ngumoha, Victor Munoz, Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola have all been very effective. The prospect of adding Hugo Ekitike to this list when he returns from injury is simply mouth-watering. Just imagine how exciting and good he will look in this side. But there's also Will Wright ready to breakthrough. Jayden Danns if he can just escape his niggles could also become an excellent option. The likes of Joshua Abe and Erik Farkas could also bolster Iraola's depth in the coming years to come. Not to mention Djylian N'Guessan has also agreed a move to Anfield. Phenomenal Keyrol Figueroa is coming to Liverpool's first-team This summer, Liverpool agreed a new contract with Keyrol Figueroa before sending him out on loan to Port Vale. During the September and October international break, Figueroa scored his first goal for Honduras in a crucial game against Jamaica, netting the winner in a 1-0 game. Last season, Figueroa only started 10 games for Liverpool's U21 side, coming on as a substitute more often, and yet he managed to score 12 goals. For Port Vale, he's now played around 227 minutes, coming off the bench five times and starting one game. In that period, he has scored three goals off the bench against Gillingham, Manchester City's U21 side and Rochdale. In total, Figueroa has scored four goals for club and country in about 354 minutes averaging a goal every 81.5 minutes in his last eight matches. He is proving he is a phenomenal goal-scorer with a great understanding for the game. With this kind of form, he will be catapulting himself to Liverpool's first-team very soon when his loan spell expires.

item.title: Disappointed Eva Olid pinpoints what her Man United Women side need to improve on after 0-0 draw
item.description: Disappointed Eva Olid pinpoints what her Man United Women side need to improve on after 0-0 draw Manchester United Women picked up another draw with Everton in the WSL. The 0-0 stalemate was a disappointing result as the Reds looked to close in on the Champions League places. In a match with very few chances, head coach Eva Olid was frankly disappointed in her side’s efforts in front of goal when she was speaking to the club’s media . Match analysis Olid explained, “for me it was a bad match. I think credit to Everton, I think that they made things difficult and how the game was going didn’t suit us. But we have to adapt because it’s not always going to be the kind of game that we want or is good for us and for how we want to play. We need to be flexible about what the opposition is doing and adapt.” The head coach admitted there were different ways of looking at the result. She said you could look at it as an away point in a tough stadium but that she wanted her side to have higher standards than that. Preparation for Aston Villa In preparation for United’s match next Sunday against Aston Villa, she explained, “we go, we speak, we try to solve what was not right today and continue. Like always we need to have conversations when the things go good, what we are doing well and today the things were not as we expected, we need to have a conversation because this cannot happen.” She explained that football is a sport where you cannot control much but you can control how you go about your work. Olid added, “you can lose, you can win, you can draw, but always being yourself and performing. Everything can happen in football, of course, but the performance always depends one-hundred per cent on us and it always has to be there, that’s the minimum.” Finally, ahead of Villa next weekend, she wants her team to work as well on and off the ball as they had been doing before yesterday’s match. The draw means that United are currently fourth in the WSL behind London City Lionesses. The Red Devils are currently four points behind them but the third placed side do have a game in hand. item.title: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United
item.description: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United What Marco Rose said after Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Leeds United quite neatly summed it all up: "I've got used to the Premier League now and I know how close everything is together and how much you have to appreciate it if you win these tight games." item.content:encoded: A big one that got away - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United What Marco Rose said after Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Leeds United quite neatly summed it all up: "I've got used to the Premier League now and I know how close everything is together and how much you have to appreciate it if you win these tight games." This one was gossamer thin. Leeds could so easily have come away from the home of a side in blistering hot form with a creditable result. The game changed and hinged on one single five-yard pass. But when you're fishing in margins this thin one single five-yard pass can decide whether or not you catch three points or a whopping great heartbreak. The first 10 minutes suggested that the recently-all-conquering Cherries were not going to have it all their own way. There was some tidy football on both flanks as the Whites got Harry Wilson and Daniel James involved high up the pitch early on. With Wilson it was neat interplay and one-twos, while James simple spun on a six pence to leave Tyler Adams sprawling, beat the next man and flashed the ball right through the danger zone. That ball was not at all far from being met by Dominic Calvert-Lewin. All the football was being played by the visitors and one move in particular cast a spell on the hosts, until VAR got them off the hook. That move began with James Trafford, progressed through Tarik Muharemović's perfect switch to the right and was carried on by Jayden Bogle and Wilson, who found James Justin on the outside. The defender's pass across the box was tucked home by Calvert-Lewin, but via his arm. VAR intervened and it stayed 0-0. The perfect response would have been to just go and score another and Leeds came close. The very next phase of play saw Wilson on the ball, cutting in from the right and firing just past the post. The Welshman's confidence and involvement grew, playing exactly where everyone envisaged him causing problems when he signed in the summer. When Ao Tanaka intercepted a poor pass in the final third Wilson was on the scene immediately, popping up on the left to link up with the midfielder, get the ball back and dart into the area where his low cross was cut out. Bournemouth had not been completely quiet in the first half an hour, James Trafford had to come sliding out to gather a potentially dangerous through ball and Leeds had to defend a corner but there was no hint of danger at all in the moments prior to the Cherries' opener. Muharemović took a goal kick, passed it to Trafford and the goalkeeper stepped forward, shaped to find Tanaka and instead gave it straight to Justin Kluivert, who duly found Evanilson. He found the net and Bournemouth had in their hands a lead that they could defend. Just about every player Farke sent onto the pitch on Saturday misplaced at least one pass, but when it's that close to goal and that decisive there is no getting away from it. It was a game-changing error. The goal appeared to wake the hosts up, too. They enjoyed more possession than before and some territory with it. Leeds had too many unnecessary turnovers from passes that weren't delivered with the right accuracy or simply weren't on to be tried. Yet there were still signs of encouragement in the latter moments of the half and the second period didn't get off to a bad start either. Good work from Gabriel Gudmundsson on the left put Leeds on the front foot, James swept the ball right to Bogle and his pass for Wilson was a touch heavy. James' pace gave Leeds the chance up the pitch quickly or break from deep, it was just the final bit missing when play got there. A team who had won their previous five games, scoring 14 times, were always going to forge chances and Trafford was called into action to beat away a Marcus Tavernier free-kick, before Rayan whistled a shot past the post. Daniel Farke's changes midway through the half saw Anton Stach, Lukas Nmecha and Sean Longstaff all join the game. Gudmundsson's exit pushed Justin to left-back and almost brought immediate dividend. Wilson dug out a cross from the right and Justin arrived back post to head just wide. The haunting thing for Leeds on Halloween was decision making and execution in and around the box, because the ball was there to be used to make something happen and rescue a result. Crosses into the area weren't quite right. Stach sent a free-kick high over the bar, then crossed too close to the keeper with Longstaff screaming for a cutback. The German set his sights from the edge of the box and his shot was just off target. When Bournemouth dispossessed Longstaff and the ball was cut through the Leeds backline for Amine Adli to tuck in an insurance goal, it was everything the visitors had needed and lacked in the second half. A little bit of magic and, crucially, a shot on target. A moment of beauty that had Farke calling the sport 'brutal' at full-time. Whether or not they would have kept up their first half momentum and actually finished off a move to win the game is another question. Rose feels 'quite sure' that Leeds will collect 'many points' this season, which will come as exactly no consolation to anyone in and around Elland Road because this was one that got away. And it would have big. The only thing to be done is to cast out into the Premier League again, tighten things up at the top end of the pitch and reel in that elusive win.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Plenty of well-deserved adjectives have been affixed to the glorious hockey career of Detroit Red Wings legendary defenseman Nicklas Lidstrom . Controversial, outspoken, and opinionated aren’t usually on the list. However, Lidstrom wasn’t pulling any punches in his reaction to news that the ban on Russia from involvement in international hockey competitions may be lifting. Nick Lidström, VP of hockey operations for Detroit, wants Sweden to boycott international tournaments if Russia participate https://t.co/uPeWzCrIV2 — Robin on the Avs 🇺🇦🇸🇪 (@AvsRobin) October 31, 2026 “The first thought is that we should boycott this,” Lidstrom told Swedish Hockey News . The IIHF was banning the Russian Ice Hockey Federation from all international competitions in February 2022 following that country’s invasion of neighboring Ukraine. Russia appealed this decision to the International Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in August. This appeal was launched after the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) Council extended a blanket ban on Russia from participating in all IIHF events. The court annulled all five IIHF Council resolutions and ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in all IIHF competitions. Expectations are that the IIHF will be launching an appeal of this decision early this week. Along with his role as vice president of hockey operations for the Red Wings, Lidstrom also serves as an advisor to the Swedish Hockey Federation (SHF). Anders Larsson, chairman of the SHF, is on record saying the country won’t boycott any international events if Russia is participating. Red Wings Russian Five Member Supports Decision Viacheslav Fetisov was part of the iconic Russian Five. He was Lidstrom’s teammate on two Red Wings Stanley Cup-winning teams. Fetisov finds himself on the opposite side of this debate from his fellow Hall of Fame defenseman. The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events. More ➡️ https://t.co/OdTH1SRTpg pic.twitter.com/1NjzvXuPUS — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 30, 2026 A member of the Russian State Duma, Fetisov naturally supports the return of his homeland to international hockey. But he thinks that they should only do it if they are all in. Fetisov wants to see Russia playing internationally as Russia. At the past two Olympic Games, Russian athletes were permitted to compete. However, they competed as Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN) without national flags, anthems, or participation in the opening ceremony parade. “Why hasn’t our country announced its desire to reintroduce national symbols on uniforms?” Fetisov told Russian website Sport-Express . “This is also unprecedented. “For some reason, we’re forgetting this important issue. item.title: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho STUNNED by Jude Bellingham's controversial Ballon d'Or ranking!
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v RB Leipzig - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has admitted his surprise after Jude Bellingham finished outside the top ten in the recent Ballon d'Or voting. The Portuguese boss praised several global stars but expressed clear frustration over his midfielder's final placement before abruptly ending his comments. Mourinho stunned by Bellingham ranking Mourinho has publicly questioned the recent Ballon d'Or voting results . The Portuguese tactician was left completely surprised by Bellingham's final position in the global standings. The England international controversially finished 11th in the prestigious awards ranking. This placement clearly baffled his club manager, who refused to elaborate further on the perceived injustice after dropping his initial comment. Bellingham has been a vital figure for Los Blancos, making his slip outside the top ten a major talking point. Mourinho ensured the media knew exactly how he felt about the final tallies. Madrid boss shares voting frustration Mourinho addressed the media to share his thoughts on the individual accolades. While he offered praise for several other global stars, the topic of Bellingham's final ranking dominated his closing remarks. "Regarding the Ballon d'Or voting, the thing that left me a bit surprised is the position of Jude Bellingham, who was eleventh," Mourinho stated on the club's official website . The Los Blancos manager made his feelings known without launching into a lengthy tirade. He simply concluded the topic by adding, "No further comments." Mourinho praises Kane and Mbappe Before expressing his disbelief over Bellingham, Mourinho took time to congratulate his former striker Harry Kane. He admitted his disappointment that a Madrid player did not win the main prize, but expressed genuine happiness for the England star to add another accolade to his career. "I had the privilege of working with Harry Kane. He is a great player, a great professional, and a great person," Mourinho explained. "Despite the frustration that my player hasn’t won, I must also be honest and say I am very happy for Harry." Mourinho also reserved special praise for forward Kylian Mbappe, highlighting his incredible international pedigree, saying: "Kylian is unique. Every year we have a Ballon d'Or, but the best player in the history of the World Cups is only one," he added. Madrid shift focus to Racing Santander Los Blancos is currently preparing for an important Liga clash against Racing Santander. Mourinho's side sit third in the league table after collecting 24 points from their opening ten matches. They currently trail league leaders Barcelona by a concerning six-point margin and cannot afford further slip-ups.

item.title: “Do Not Believe USC is Going to Be Able to Humble Themselves”: Radio Host Claims Trojans Should Hire ‘Non-P4’ Coach if Lincoln Riley Gets Fired
item.description: Lincoln Riley © Instagram/uscfb Lincoln Riley’s time at USC seems to be coming to an end after yet another disappointing season for the Trojans, and they will likely fail to make the CFP. Right now, the Trojans are unranked, are 6-2, and face their toughest game of the season so far this Saturday against the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes. Many in Los Angeles and in college football more broadly are starting to ask who could be USC’s next coach. Analyst Brock Vereen believes that if the Trojans part ways with Riley after the 2026 season, they should look outside the Power Four conferences to find a new head coach. He just doesn’t believe they will bring themselves to do so. Here’s what he said about the matter on Saturday via 97.1 The Fan’s X : “I would want a head coach who is currently at a non-power conference school, I just do not believe USC is going to be able to humble themselves to make that call!” He also mentioned Jason Eck as the top coach he would like to see at USC, calling the New Mexico coach the dream choice for the Trojans. However, he clarified that if the Wisconsin job becomes available, Eck would likely want to go to his alma mater. Lincoln Riley wants to stay at USC for the foreseeable future Lincoln Riley is convinced his future lies with the Trojans. Despite the backlash from the fandom in recent weeks, Riley made it clear this Tuesday to the press that he sees himself at USC in the foreseeable future: “Listen, if I didn’t want to be at this place, I wouldn’t have come here in the first place. I’ve had plenty of opportunities to leave,” Riley said Tuesday afternoon. “This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I’m the right person to be here. And that’s as honest and transparent as I can be with you guys. “I love it here. I mean like I told you guys a lot of times — there’s not many people in college football history that gave up what I gave up to come here, I don’t care if it’s 15 years down the line, that never should be taken lightly. It’s certainly not taken lightly by me. I came here because I believe in this place and none of that has changed whatsoever.” Much of his job security likely rides on the result of Saturday’s game. item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ‘92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 goals in a season for Notts County. item.title: If Mikel Arteta’s dossier is part of a deliberate strategy, it is a dangerous one for Arsenal | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
